entries.label: Final
entries.headline: Ravens pour it on late as Commanders fall 41-3 in preseason finale
entries.body:
Quick programming note before we get into it: this game blog is a day late because of a size issue. Specifically, the digest generation pipeline had a size issue. The Commanders also had a size issue of their own on offense Friday night, scoring a total of 3 points, but I swear the two are unrelated.

The fourth quarter opened with Washington still trying to find any kind of footing, and it did not take long for things to get worse. After a Commanders punt [1], Baltimore's D.McMillan broke a 63-yard run to set up shop at the Washington 19 [2]. A shotgun snap then went haywire, with C.Bullock fumbling the aborted attempt and the Ravens recovering right back at the WAS 19 [3]. Two plays later A.Reed found C.Johnson for a 20-yard touchdown, and the extra point made it a laugher, pushing the score to 41-3 [4]. Per @JPFinlayNBCS, Robert Henry summed up the effort as coming out "juiceless" and spending the rest of the game trying to catch up [45], which tracked with everything that followed.

From there the quarter settled into survival mode for Washington. Sam Hartman and the offense strung together a few short completions, including gains to L.Cager [8, 28, 31] and J.Jones [17], and a 12-yard pitch and catch to J.Bradley [30], but nothing came close to points. A promising-looking drive for Baltimore that featured Robert Henry chewing up yardage on the ground [18, 19, 20, 21] eventually stalled when Hartman was sacked [22] and Washington's defense held before another punt [26]. The final stretch was pure clock management, with C.Reynolds grinding out a handful of short runs [29, 33, 34, 35] into the two-minute warning [32] before time expired on a 41-3 final [36]. Dan Quinn didn't sugarcoat it afterward, telling reporters the night "was not good enough" and "not indicative of the last 6 weeks," which "pisses me off," per @NickiJhabvala [40], while @john_keim relayed the coach calling the performance below standard regardless of who was on the field [38, 41].

finalThoughts.headline: Commanders Close Out Preseason by Getting Fully Ratio'd, Defense Politely Requests a Trip to the Glue Factory
finalThoughts.body:
This one was over before most fans finished their first beer. Baltimore scored on a reversed touchdown call in the first quarter [10], added a quick fullback punch-in a few drives later [19], and by halftime John Keim was reporting a 24-0 lead built on a jaw-dropping 17-1 first down disparity and a 274-60 yardage gap [206]. Nicki Jhabvala noted the Commanders had all of two first downs through two and a half quarters, and one of those came via penalty [200]. That is not a slow start, that is a team that forgot the ball was oblong.

What went right could fit on an index card. Drew Stevens' 39-yard field goal in the third quarter accounted for the only Washington points of the night [123], prompting Seth to sarcastically note it was "only 31-3 Ravens" as if that qualified as progress [195, 196]. Luke McCaffrey made a genuinely nice adjustment on a high, behind-him throw that JP Finlay singled out as the kind of play a fringe roster guy needs to make in game three [209]. Beyond that, the highlights folder is mostly empty.

What went wrong is basically everything else. Darius Rush had what Finlay bluntly called a rough night [208], the defense surrendered a 63-yard run to Devin McMillan that set up another Baltimore score [141, 143], and Jaden Bradley fumbled a kickoff return that Washington recovered by the skin of its teeth [68, 207]. Drew Stevens also missed a 62-yard attempt short and wide, which Ben Standig and John Keim both dryly noted despite his supposedly strong leg [38, 211, 212, 214, 215]. Seth summed up the defensive performance by comparing it to a horse headed for the glue factory [193, 194], and Dan Quinn himself admitted postgame that "it wasn't good enough" and "wasn't up to our standards" [177, 179].

The shape of the game never really changed hands. Baltimore controlled it from the opening kickoff return that gained 30 yards [1] straight through to the final whistle, piling up touchdowns in every quarter [10, 19, 108, 143] while Washington's offense sputtered behind missed kicks, penalties, and a defense that could not get off the field. Robert Henry said the team came out "juiceless" and spent the whole game trying to catch up [184], which is as tidy a summary as any for a 41-3 defeat that closed out the preseason on the sourest possible note.
finalThoughts.heroReason: He is responsible for literally all three Commanders points via his 39-yard field goal [123], a bar so low it is technically underground, but someone had to clear it.
finalThoughts.goatReason: JP Finlay flagged him by name for a rough night [208], and he later drew an Illegal Touch Kick penalty on a punt he should have just let bounce [115], because apparently touching things he shouldn't touch was the theme of his evening.
